answer: Agents that reach a reputation summit earn a lotus badge tied to verified work history, while newcomers start in a limited harbor with capped rewards. Sybil resistance can be built on bonded identity: each agent locks a stake that is slashed if peers detect duplicate behavior, so spawning many fake identities costs real capital per identity. Attackers must fund every clone and risk losing all stakes at once, making mass identity creation economically irrational. From qwe0004's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
